title: Obstacle Course
strapline: Over, under, through and along — a body-sized problem to solve.
intent: A changing obstacle course invites big, whole-body movement — climbing, crawling, balancing, jumping — that builds strength and coordination.
Negotiating space and equipment develops spatial awareness and careful, planned movement.
Assessing "can I do that?" and having a go grows confidence and healthy risk-taking.
Working out the best route is a real physical problem to think through and solve.
Waiting for a turn and cheering others on builds patience and belonging.
implementation: Set out a route with things to go over, under, through, along and around, and change it often.
Include a real balance challenge (a beam, a plank, a line of tyres) at a height children can manage.
Model the movements and the safety — "hold on here", "look where your feet go" — then step back.
Let children help design and rebuild the course so it is theirs, not yours.
Talk the positional language as they move: over, under, through, between, along.
Keep group sizes sensible so children keep moving rather than queueing.
Add a timer or a "beat your own go" element for children who want a challenge.
key_questions: How will you get over/under/through this part?
Where will you put your hands and feet to stay balanced?
Can you find a different way round?
What could we add to make it trickier?
How can we all have a safe turn?

impact.text: Children run, climb, balance and negotiate obstacles with growing control and confidence.
Children plan a route and keep trying until they manage a tricky part.
Children use and understand positional language as they move through the course.
Children take safe risks and grow in physical self-belief.
Children take turns and encourage one another through the course.

enhancements: Crates, planks, tyres, tunnels and low beams that can be rearranged.
Stepping stones or spots for balancing and jumping targets.
A-frames or a low climbing structure for going over.
Cones, hoops and arrows to mark the route and direction.
A visual "how to build it" card so children can set it up themselves.
A stopwatch or sand timer for an optional personal challenge.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into big physical play and test what their bodies can do.
active_learning: Children persist through the tricky sections and take pride in completing the course.
creating_thinking: Children plan and adapt their route, and invent new challenges to add.
